review_reason: This is a direct, concrete instance of the named weak spot: a column-alignment table-detection heuristic could misfire on the ASCII box-drawing terminal banner inside a fenced code block. Per task instructions, any entry related to false-positive table risk must be explicitly reviewed, not rubber-stamped.

expected_no_table_zones.location: lines 90-111, inside a ```console fenced code block under '### Run it'
expected_no_table_zones.looks_like: a bordered table or multi-column layout
expected_no_table_zones.reason: A genuine ASCII box-drawing UI mockup of the `fastapi dev` CLI startup banner, using Unicode box-drawing characters (U+2502 '│' vertical line, U+256D/U+2570 rounded corners, U+2500 horizontal line) to draw a single decorative box, NOT a table. Verified directly: the vertical bar character used is U+2502 (BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL), NOT the ASCII pipe U+007C used in real markdown tables -- a character-level check would correctly distinguish these, but a purely VISUAL/column-alignment heuristic (looking for repeated vertically-aligned delimiter-like characters across consecutive lines) could still misfire, since the │ characters genuinely do line up in vertical columns across 8 consecutive lines, which is structurally exactly what a column-alignment table heuristic looks for. This is the closest real-world analogue to the 'architecture diagrams' false-positive risk named explicitly in the task brief.

expected_noise_elements: 3 fenced code blocks total (console/Python/JSON), one of which is the ASCII diagram described above -- all code block content should be excluded from heading/table structural analysis entirely, being verbatim code, not document structure
notes_for_implementer: PRIMARY test target for named weak spot #2 in a non-HTML context: verify Pith does NOT report a table for the ASCII box-drawing banner in the '### Run it' section. The critical distinguishing signal available to Pith is that this entire block sits inside a fenced ```console code block -- if Pith's structure-inference runs on raw text without first respecting code-fence boundaries, it is much more likely to misinterpret the box-drawing characters as tabular columns. A correct implementation should treat fenced code block content as opaque/literal and never apply table or heading detection inside it at all. This is a cleaner, more isolated version of the same false-positive risk pattern found embedded in fixture 19's ASCII network-protocol diagrams (which are NOT inside a code fence, making that fixture a harder version of the same test).
